descriptionChirho: To harbor persistent enmity, bear a grudge, or cherish animosity against someone, expressing deep-seated hostile feelings that may manifest in persecutory action. All six occurrences are Qal stem with consistent semantic range. Used of Esau's grudge against Jacob over the stolen blessing (Gen 27:41), of Joseph's brothers fearing his lasting resentment (Gen 49:23; 50:15), of enemies bearing malice against the psalmist (Ps 55:3), and of God's perceived hostility in Job's complaints (Job 16:9, 30:21). Arabic glosses consistently use forms of 'abghada' (hate) and 'aadaa' (be hostile); Korean uses 'miwohada' (hate); Hindi uses 'bair rakhna' (bear enmity) throughout.
